title: Shareable Initiatives
intent: Publish and fetch the Initiative refs the way Work manifests already are, so an Initiative is repository state rather than machine state.
motivation: An Initiative holds the intent, the motivation for a breakdown, and the ordering — the reasoning a flat Work list never carried. None of it is pushed today, so a clone sees seven Works belonging to an Initiative it cannot read. Worse, Initiative numbers are minted from what exists locally, so a second clone mints a number that is already taken and two Initiatives collide on one identifier. That failure had to be repaired by hand once already.
ordering: One Work: the gap is a single namespace missing from one adapter, and splitting the push from the fetch would leave a half-shareable Initiative that is harder to reason about than either end state.
